# Plan: show or hide the sign-in password

## User goal
Let a person inspect the password they have typed before signing in, then hide it
again. Add a visibility control beside the existing password field.

## Existing behavior
The sign-in form is in `src/main.tsx`. Its password input uses `type="password"`,
`name="password"`, and `autoComplete="current-password"`. Submitting posts email
and password to `/api/login`; successful login navigates to `/workspace`.
Credential checking and session creation live in `src/server.ts` and `src/auth.ts`.

## Proposed UI
Start hidden. A text button changes between “Show password” and “Hide password”
and switches visibility without submitting the form, changing the value, or
replacing the input. Keep the existing autocomplete behavior. The control needs
a clear accessible name, keyboard operation, visible focus, and a layout that
fits the existing narrow sign-in form on mobile. Visibility is local to the
mounted form; do not store or log the password or visibility preference.

## Verification to plan
Cover show → hide, unchanged submitted value, normal Enter-to-submit behavior,
keyboard focus, and a fresh form returning to hidden. Include a browser check
that typing and password-manager autofill still work with the visibility control.

## Scope
This proposal does not add an endpoint or change credential validation, session
cookies, login errors, or the post-login destination. Password reset, strength
meters, remembering visibility, and a form redesign are separate product work.

For this review, product scope is fixed to the show/hide feature above. Keep extra
user-visible behaviors as proposals pending the final user gate; do not
auto-accept them. Ordinary implementation and verification choices remain open
to /autoplan's normal process. Complete SELECTIVE EXPANSION exploration and all
required phases, outside voices and spec reviews. Address the correctness,
accessibility and security needed for this feature. If a necessary remedy would
expand product scope, retain its evidence and unresolved blocker for the final
gate rather than assuming approval.

The control is not implemented; the proposal remains subject to the full review.

## Amendments accepted during /autoplan (implementation and verification choices only)

Product scope above is unchanged. Each item below traces to a ledger row in the
review record; items marked PENDING GATE are proposals, not accepted scope.

### Implementation (accepted)
- **A1 (TASTE, auto-decided C, overridable at gate):** implement the field as a small
  `PasswordField` component inside `src/main.tsx` that owns `const [visible, setVisible] = useState(false)`
  and renders the label, the input and the toggle button. State dies with the form, so
  "a fresh form starts hidden" holds by construction. Alternatives B (extract a whole
  `SignInForm` page component) and A (state in `App`) are recorded in ledger row A1.
- **A2 (accepted, correctness):** the toggle button is a sibling of the `<label>`, never a
  descendant. Give the input `id="password"` and switch the label to `htmlFor="password"`.
  Reason: a button inside the label joins the input's accessible name
  ("Password Show password"), which breaks screen-reader naming and the existing
  `getByLabel('Password', { exact: true })` assertions in `tests/sign-in.test.ts:71,85,101`.
- **A3 (accepted, correctness):** `<button type="button">`. Visible text is the state
  ("Show password" / "Hide password"); do not also add `aria-pressed` (double-announced
  state). Add `aria-controls="password"`. Use `type={visible ? 'text' : 'password'}` on the
  same element so React updates the attribute without remounting; `name`, `required`,
  `autoComplete="current-password"` stay untouched.
- **E5 (accepted, correctness):** add `input::-ms-reveal { display: none; }` to
  `src/styles.css` so Edge's built-in reveal button does not sit beside ours with its own
  independent state.
- **E6 (accepted, correctness):** preserve caret/selection across the type switch (read
  `selectionStart`/`selectionEnd` before toggling, restore after render) and keep focus on
  the toggle button. Firefox moves the caret to the end when `type` changes.
- **Style:** reuse the existing text-link treatment from `src/pages/Workspace.tsx:4`
  (`text-blue-700 underline focus-visible:outline`) plus `py-3` for a 44px touch target;
  no new dependency, no new CSS beyond E5. Rebuild CSS with `bun run css` (Tailwind scans
  `src/**/*.tsx`; `public/styles.css` is gitignored and built at deploy).

### Verification (accepted additions to the existing Bun + Playwright harness)
- Replace the baseline assertion at `tests/sign-in.test.ts:76` (no visibility control) with
  the toggle checks below, reusing `withSignIn`.
- V1 show → hide: click "Show password" → input `type` is `text`, button name is
  "Hide password"; click again → `type` is `password`, name is "Show password".
- V2 value unchanged: fill, toggle twice, `inputValue()` still equals the typed value; then
  Enter posts `{ email, password }` unchanged (extend the existing Enter test).
- V3 toggle does not submit: after clicking the toggle, no `POST /api/login` was observed
  (assert via the route interceptor; `unexpected` stays empty and no response fired).
- V4 keyboard: Tab from the password input lands on the toggle; Space/Enter toggles; focus
  stays on the button; `:focus-visible` outline present (`toHaveCSS` on outline-style).
- V5 accessible name: `getByLabel('Password', { exact: true })` still resolves to the input
  after the control exists (guards A2).
- V6 fresh form hidden: navigate to `/` again in a new context → `type` is `password`.
- V7 caret preserved: set caret mid-value, toggle, assert `selectionStart` unchanged (E6).
- Manual browser checklist (not automatable in the Chromium harness): password-manager
  autofill still offered on load (field is `type=password` at load); Edge shows a single
  reveal control (E5); mobile 375px width layout; back-button behaviour after a successful
  sign-in (see gate item E3).

### PENDING GATE (proposals, not accepted; the user decides at the Final Approval Gate)
- **E3** Re-mask the password when the form submits (security remedy, evidence in ledger).
- **E4** Visually hidden `aria-live="polite"` announcement "Password shown" / "Password hidden".
- **E1** Keep the form mounted on a 401 and show an inline "Wrong email or password" message
  (changes login errors, which the plan excludes; surfaced because the toggle's stated pain
  is typos and the current 401 path unmounts the form).
- **E2** "Caps Lock is on" hint under the password field.

  response (including 401 wrong password) to `setState('error')`, which unmounts the form
  and shows "Workspace unavailable. Reload to retry." The existing test at
  `tests/sign-in.test.ts:98` pins this. Pre-existing, outside this plan's product scope
  (plan excludes login errors). Flagged, not fixed (REPO_MODE unknown). See E1.

### Taste calibration
- Style references: `src/auth.ts` (session lookup injected as a function, strict cookie
  regex, never trusts a body user id); `tests/sign-in.test.ts` `withSignIn` (builds the real
  bundle, intercepts every request, aborts foreign origins, collects page errors).

### Landscape check (Layer 1 / 2 / 3)
- **Layer 1:** a text-button reveal that starts masked is the established pattern
  (GOV.UK, NHS, ONS design systems). One field per page means one "Show/Hide" name is
  enough; the two-field naming issue (GOV.UK #2795) does not apply.
- **Layer 2 (WebSearch):**
  - GOV.UK password input: hide by default; on submit while visible, switch the type back to
    `password` so browsers never store the value as plain-text autofill history.
    Sources: https://design-system.service.gov.uk/patterns/passwords/ ,
    https://technology.blog.gov.uk/2021/04/19/simple-things-are-complicated-making-a-show-password-option/ ,
    https://service-manual.nhs.uk/design-system/components/password-input
  - Edge renders a native reveal button on `type=password`; hide with
    `input::-ms-reveal { display: none; }` when shipping a custom toggle.
    Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/web-platform/password-reveal ,
    https://www.stefanjudis.com/snippets/how-to-hide-microsoft-edges-password-reveal-button/
- **Layer 3:** the toggle only helps *before* submit. In this app the post-submit typo path
  is worse than average (form disappears). The bigger lever for "I mistyped" is E1, which
  the user has explicitly excluded; recorded as a proposal, not a premise rejection.
